children: Challenger's capital returns and offshore growth opportunities are largely priced in at the Australian investment manager's current valuation, Macquarie analysts say. With an unchanged neutral rating on the stock, the analysts tell clients in a note that its near-term share-price upside looks limited. They point out that the stock is trading at 13.9 times 12-month forward earnings, compared with a three-year average of 11.9 times. Short interest in the stock is also near record lows, they add. Macquarie trims its target price on the stock by 5.9% to 9.60 Australian dollars. Shares are up 3.1% at A$10.10. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
